why: Run 1's brief, fixed at C_K, omits generator steps that holon derive --milestone M3 needs. One is holon disch --milestone M3: derive's typed part refuses unless gen/M3/disch/closure.json and conjuncts.json are fresh holon disch output. The other is the authoring of the DISCH, UNDO and FACT sidecars, without any one of which derive refuses as a whole. The brief also orders holon lossy before holon run, which writes the model lossy reads, and runs replay only when its help names a milestone, which it never does. In run 1, derive wrote no law and 0 statements were matched. The cause is the instrument, not HOLON. Run 1's brief is unchanged (R0's pin holds), and run 1 scores the preregistered predictions. Run 2's corrected brief is spec/M3/lib/blind_session_r2.md. It adds holon disch, and the authoring of the DISCH, UNDO and FACT sidecars, before derive. It names derive's optional parts (OWN, NAT and PAR-init, link_domain and the bundle laws), moves lossy after run, and drops the local replay (the runners' final filter replays). It also states that M2's derive reads hand-written facts, which the session logs as not_reproducible. Run 2's agreement is the comparison of record for the exit section, disclosed as an amended rerun. No prediction or threshold changes.

The preregistered reads check judges text, not reads. It flags any input that names a forbidden root, and any absolute-looking substring of a shell command. In run 1 it flagged 7 items in 4 calls: a grep pattern, and the sed rewrite of config/holon.json's /root/work/morph value that the brief requires (calls 10 and 11); and two grep regexes it took for paths (calls 105 and 117). None of the four opened anything outside W. The amended scorer, tests_m3/_i46_reads.py::reads_problems, judges actual reads: file-tool paths, the file operands of shell commands (not patterns or scripts), redirection targets, cd and -C directories, and absolute path literals in inline code. It scores run 1 at 0 problems against the old scorer's 7, and it catches synthetic reads outside W. calls_problems is unchanged and still scores P2 and E5 as preregistered (run 1: fail). Run 2 is scored with both scorers, and both verdicts are reported. No prediction or threshold changes.

The pack and the scope set leave out spec/ledger/assumptions.json, and holon run writes no record without it: records.v2_fields -> resolve_bundle -> all_bundles -> load_ledger raised FileNotFoundError on the par job's first law in both of run 2's step-5 runs, so run 2's 195 M3 laws have no record and I82's status metric matched 0 of the lead's 257 M3 classes. The ledger is the model-assumption catalogue. For each of three hand-written facts bundles (morph_header, morph_rollup, morph_batchdata) it lists the assumption entries (id, kind, source, text, and the model definitions that introduce them) and the no_assumption groups that classify the model's other definitions, plus one encoding note. A record's model_assumptions are the ids of the entries its cone meets, and no status is computed from the ledger. It holds no M3 law, statement or status. On the coordinator's ruling, run 2's scope set gains this one file. It is given as it is at c3eda197 (16220 bytes, sha256 37e311b2f16d5d7b708b33ceaecceaa216947e2d9e0b403655ab765ff1b6187e, the same at this head), at SCOPE/files/spec/ledger/assumptions.json, and SCOPE/stripped.json lists it with no stripped key. audit/blind/I46/run2/scope/ records the amended set. It is given unstripped: the scope's strip rules would remove its bundles list whole (a list is removed whole), and load_ledger reads that list. The reasons are leak:case_id (D2), leak:code_site (Rollup.sol:24, Rollup.sol:25 twice, Rollup.sol:188-195, common/blob/payload.go:22), leak:law_name (L_dom_hdr, L_fact_Z, L_nat_eta2, none of them an M3 law) and leak:section_ref (§11.6). These 10 matches sit in three free-text fields: entry Hyp-Z0-kzg's text and two no_assumption whys. Those fields and two more free-text fields also hold result-like phrases about M0 to M2: hypothesis Z0's 'status checked', the M1 replay corpus's '0 disagreements', the 'L_dom_hdr witness', the 'L_nat_eta2 witness traces', and a Go size-class table that is 'wrong for real Go'. No record field is computed from a free-text field. The blind session copies the file into place itself and re-runs its brief from step 5: the par job's run, lean and run under the pack's budgets, then lossy and done.json. Every other M3 law goes to the runners, as the protocol says. Run 1's scoring is unchanged, and no prediction or threshold changes.

Amends line 3's disclosure. On the coordinator's ruling, run 2 is not given spec/ledger/assumptions.json as it is at c3eda197. It is given its redaction by tests_m3/blind_ledger.py --commit c3eda197 (14778 bytes, sha256 379bcb48d1595e3fc559a1a8ed94ea97303f41384d92a2040977c3e4bca2f27b). Every doc, text and why string, 40 members in all, is replaced by one fixed marker, and every other member is unchanged. The redaction removes the 10 leak-class matches and the result-like phrases about M0 to M2 that line 3 lists. The scope's strip rules strip nothing from the given file, and the script checks this, and that the other members equal the source's. Records are computed from members it leaves unchanged: each bundle's facts, facts_sha256 and model, each entry's id, introduced_by and requires, and each no_assumption group's defs. So their model_assumptions and ledger_match are those of the full ledger. SCOPE/stripped.json lists the 40 blanked key paths for the file, and audit/blind/I46/run2/scope/ records them with the script, its rule and the marker. The unredacted file was in SCOPE from 21:31 to 21:38 UTC, until this swap, and the blind session was not resumed in that time: W/spec/ledger did not exist, and the session's log was last written at 21:07. The resume text tells the session that the blanked members are not authored inputs, although stripped.json lists them. No prediction or threshold changes.
